payload.headline: Meta slips 0.4% to 616.38, still stuck between support and resistance before January earnings

summary.thesis: Meta's sales are still growing fast, but free cash flow fell from 44.8B to 28.6B, and the 616.38 price assumes it recovers quickly.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait. Swing: wait. The 2027-01-27 report on margins and cash flow is the event that decides this.
summary.act_at: Buy near 475.85; trim above 707.21; swing only on a hold of 605.33–611.95 or a close above 648.45

payload.happening: Meta closed at 616.38, down 0.4%. It remains in a downtrend, below its 20-day (625.29), 50-day (679.29) and 200-day (628.79) averages. It sits between support at 605.33–611.95 and resistance starting at 622.66. The only news was two Instagram stories from The Verge: one reported that the 'school safety' push was also a way to bring more teens onto the app, and one covered a small feature that lets users edit stories after posting. The next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
payload.business: Demand is healthy. Sales grew 27.53% over the last year to 241.6B, though quarterly growth slowed to 26.07% from 33.08% two quarters ago. Margins and cash are what changed. Operating margin (the share of sales left after running costs) fell to 32.86% from 43.23%. Free cash flow (cash left after spending on the business) dropped to 28.6B from 44.8B, only 11.86% of sales. R&D now takes 31.68% of revenue. Debt of 83.7B against cash of 11.2B leaves net cash at -1.2B. The company can still pay its bills, with 82.4B of liquidity (cash plus available borrowing), but the cushion is thinner. The filings flag that profit per share is lagging sales and that the company missed forecasts by 29% last quarter. Today's Instagram teen story affects sentiment and governance, not the numbers. It adds to concerns about how Meta handles young users (general knowledge) and could draw regulators (general knowledge). The small product update changes nothing material. What is at risk is how quickly heavy spending turns back into cash. Ad demand and the 81.03% gross margin are not at risk.

worth.text: A DCF (discounted cash flow: today's value of future cash) starts from the 28.6B of free cash flow. It gives 239.58 in the bear case, 365.9 in the base case and 496.0 in the bull case, all below 616.38. To justify today's price, free cash flow would have to start growing at about 37.9% a year. Even 30% starting growth gives only 461.81. If operating margin slid to 24%, value would be 237.13. Meta's own price-to-sales history (price relative to yearly sales) tells a kinder story. Its 5-year range gives 475.85 at the low end, 707.21 in the middle and 881.21 at the high end. The current price-to-sales of 6.6 sits at the 38.0 percentile of its own 5-year history. That is close to the peer median of 6.1 and about level with peers after adjusting for growth (1.02). The gap between the two methods comes down to one assumption: the DCF treats today's depressed cash flow as the starting point, while the history method assumes Meta returns to its usual relationship between sales and value.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow recovers toward the earlier 44.8B as the spending pays off, instead of staying near 28.6B.

bull: Sales are still growing 27.53% a year, with a 3-year sales growth rate of 23.92%, at a scale of 241.6B in revenue.
Gross margin of 81.03% shows the core ad business still converts sales efficiently. The fall in profit comes from spending, not weaker pricing.
At 6.6 times sales, Meta is near the peer median of 6.1, level with peers after adjusting for growth (1.02), and at only the 38.0 percentile of its own 5-year range.
bear: Free cash flow fell to 28.6B from 44.8B, and the price needs about 37.9% starting cash-flow growth to make sense on a DCF basis.
Operating margin dropped to 32.86% from 43.23%, and the company missed forecasts by 29% last quarter.
The trend is down: the price is below the 50-day average of 679.29, the committee call is Reduce, and the business grade is C.

levels.what: Bottom of the nearer support zone (605.33–611.95). A close below it opens the stronger zone at 591.53–598.97, which has 6 touches.
Low end of Meta's own price-to-sales history and close to the 461.81 DCF value at 30% growth. Buying here does not depend on a full margin recovery.
Midpoint of Meta's own history. Above it, the price treats the cash-flow recovery as already done, so trimming would be the action there.

longterm.why: 616.38 is above every DCF value (the highest is 496.0), the business is graded C, and the committee call is Reduce. Buying now means paying in advance for a cash-flow recovery that has not shown up yet.

swing.why: The price is between support at 611.95 and resistance at 622.66, a gap smaller than one typical daily move (ATR, the average daily range, is 21.24). That leaves too little room for a sensible stop and target. Enter only if the price holds 605.33–611.95 or closes above 648.45.

decision.timing: Options price a 10.3% move by Dec 18 and an 18.0% move by Feb 19, which includes the 2027-01-27 report. That report is the deciding event, so no long-term entry before it unless the price reaches 475.85 first.

change_mind: The 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin climbing back toward 43.23% and free cash flow moving back toward 44.8B. That would support moving the decision toward buying near support at 591.53–598.97.
A close above 648.45, the top of the second resistance zone, would break the pattern of lower highs and turn the swing view to enter.
A close below 591.53 would break both support zones and point toward 475.85 as the next long-term buy level.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait. The price is 616.38, still between support at 605.33–611.95 and resistance at 622.66, and today brought no new filing, only reported Instagram news.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
